comments.author: Ok_Map5721
comments.body: No one will tell you this, friend. Everyone is on their own. I’ve tried many times here to find out from people whether they actually found something or not. Most just hand out clever advice and advertise their tests that lead nowhere. Each man is the smith of his own fortune.

replies.author: RobodOfficial
replies.body:
That’s a fair point. A lot of strategies look impressive in backtests but fall apart in live markets once fees, slippage, and changing market conditions come into play.  
I think the bigger problem isn’t finding another AI trading tool. It’s learning how to properly validate a strategy before trusting it with real money. A profitable backtest alone doesn’t prove anything.  
But here’s something worth thinking about. If someone spends months researching, testing, and building something useful, and the moment they share it, we call it advertising, what exactly are we expecting them to do?  
And if we’re asking people to share their hard-earned knowledge and strategies, shouldn’t we also ask what we’re bringing to the table?  
There’s a big difference between empty promotion and someone genuinely trying to solve a problem. Both shouldn’t be treated the same way.  
Skepticism is healthy. Dismissing everything as advertising isn’t always fair either.

replies.author: Ok_Map5721
replies.body: Completely agree with you, friend — that’s exactly how it is. I spent months designing and building a proper bot that doesn’t just lose money. I spent months putting together a real backtest that at least doesn’t paint me pretty pictures I can later brag about here and tell everyone how great I am. Right now I’m focused only on finding a strategy. I’ve already overpaid for everything and I’m still at it. I hope I find something — and I wish the same for you.

comments.author: BenchifyAppDNS
comments.body:
Man, I have tried for months to get something going. But the biggest problem is that backtest mean very little. 

I've had live agents running for months and some have defeated the S&P for months now. But the problem is that it could be fully random. 

For example, one agent got lucky and bought CRWD before it had a huge runup because of a cybersecurity incident. Was it luck? I can't know unless I have way more data.

I don't want to send links. But if you want, I can send you a bunch of things I have learnt like PEAD or that free cash flow yield tends to be better than P/E to predict future growth.

replies.author: Ok_Map5721
replies.body: Interesting information. Would you be willing to share some of it and send me something so we can exchange experience? Write me in private if you’re up for it — we can try to brainstorm together. I’ll look at your data and send you what I have.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I can't speak to anyone's live results, but one thing that helps is to have the AI write the rules and let a separate test judge them. Check the result after fees and keep some recent data you never tuned on, because AI-built strategies often look great on the data they were built from. Start small or in paper mode before real money. Cymetica's Backtest Labs includes fees and can hold out the last part of the history for that kind of check.

I’ve had some great results and am currently rinsing the prop firms for capital. Most strategies will be tough to run on less than a 5k live account. Good luck!
